title: Task automation and instructional planning support with large language models: a systematic review
extended_summary:
This paper reviews the emerging literature on large language models (LLMs) in educational settings, focusing on whether they reduce teacher workload and support instructional planning. The review is framed around two questions: whether LLMs reduce the time spent generating educational content and improve the perceived quality of that content, and whether they automate teaching-related tasks and planning compared with traditional methods.

The review included 16 studies published between 2023 and 2025, consisting of 13 primary empirical studies and 3 secondary syntheses. The primary studies covered qualitative, quantitative, quasi-experimental, and mixed-methods designs and were concentrated mainly in higher education, with some evidence spanning mixed settings and teacher-training contexts. The LLMs studied included ChatGPT variants and other models such as GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude, LLaMA, PALM, and custom systems, and they were used for generating lessons, explanations, assessments, feedback, summaries, and other instructional materials.

Across the reviewed studies, LLMs were generally associated with reported time savings, quicker drafting of content, and perceived improvements in clarity or usefulness of generated materials. They also appeared useful for automating first-pass feedback, lesson planning, and task generation. However, the evidence was heterogeneous, often self-reported, and methodologically limited; the review highlights risks such as prompt sensitivity, hallucinations, privacy concerns, and weak reproducibility. The authors conclude that LLMs may support educators, but their use should remain human-in-the-loop and guided by clearer pedagogical frameworks and stronger evaluation designs.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s GPT-based conversational generative AI tool used for text generation, feedback, and instructional support.
identified_tools.use_case: This systematic review examined ChatGPT and other LLMs as teacher-facing tools for generating educational content, automated feedback, lesson planning, and assessment support. The paper explicitly distinguished teacher-facing uses from student-facing tutoring or learning assistance, noting that some included studies used ChatGPT for student learning tasks rather than teacher workflow support.

findings.finding_summary: Across the reviewed studies, ChatGPT-supported workflows were associated with reported reductions in time required to generate educational materials or produce feedback, but the magnitude of time savings varied by task and context and was not measured consistently. The review emphasizes that evidence is mostly self-reported, heterogeneous, and concentrated in higher-education settings, so conclusions should be interpreted cautiously.
findings.measure: Time devoted to content generation; reported efficiency/time savings for feedback and planning tasks

findings.finding_summary: The review found that ChatGPT was used for teacher-facing content generation, including lesson materials, outlines, guides, feedback, assessment items, and instructional planning support. Reported benefits were perceived clarity, usefulness, and convenience of generated resources, but outcomes were heterogeneous and often based on teacher or learner perceptions rather than objective measures.
findings.measure: Perceived quality/usefulness/clarity of generated educational materials; planning support; automated feedback generation

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review of mostly qualitative, mixed-methods, and quasi-experimental studies with heterogeneous measures and several unclear risk-of-bias domains. The paper does not provide pooled effect sizes for ChatGPT-specific outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports practical benefits such as time savings and improved perceived usefulness, but the effects are not quantified consistently and are largely based on self-report. That makes the impact direction favorable but the magnitude unclear.
